value_label: Only administrative regulations under a non-labor statute apply
note: Labor terms sit in regulations under the Act for Distant Water Fisheries (Art. 26), outside the Labor Standards Act. A pending civil case (the Yu Fu case, hearings 2025) argues the Labor Standards Act should apply.
source: Act for Distant Water Fisheries 2016; NYCU Transit Asia court observation 2025

value_label: A separate floor applies that is lower than, or not linked to, the national minimum
note: The Regulations set a minimum of US$550 a month, adjustable by annual announcement (Art. 6-1(2), added 18 Nov 2025). US$570 for crew newly recruited from 2026 is reported by the Ministry of Agriculture, but the Fisheries Agency notice could not be found or reached (rechecked 13 Nov 2026), so that figure is unverified. Both are well below Taiwan's national minimum wage under the Minimum Wage Act (in force 1 Jan 2024; NT$29,500 a month in 2026, rising to NT$30,900 from 1 Jan 2027, per the Ministry of Labor).
source: Overseas Employment Regulations Art. 6-1(2) (amended 18 Nov 2025); Minimum Wage Act; Ministry of Agriculture annual report 2025; Focus Taiwan, 6 Jan 2026

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: At least 10 hours of rest in any 24 (6 of them consecutive) and 77 hours in any 7 days, benchmarked to ILO C188; temporary exceptions with compensatory rest; no limit on hours as such.
source: Overseas Employment Regulations Art. 6(1)(7); ICSF Samudra 88 (2022)

value_label: Cannot change without the employer's consent
note: Contracts are with the vessel operator through an overseas agency. A transfer procedure exists, but only with the former operator's signed release, so crew cannot change employer without consent. Agencies may not force a transfer.
source: Overseas Employment Regulations Arts 4, 13(2)(6), 24, 25

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: No statutory bar, but crew who never enter Taiwan's labor market cannot in practice join a Taiwanese union. Indonesian unions seek a bilateral agreement.
source: Focus Taiwan, 1 Mar 2024

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are prohibited in the destination's law
note: The Regulations bar agencies from charging crew service or recruitment fees and from withholding wages as a penalty, bar operators from making crew bear recruitment costs or keeping passports (safekeeping with consent allowed), and require full, direct wage payment. Recoded from 1 to 2 after checking the text; NGOs still report deposits and deductions in practice, which this de jure code does not capture.
source: Overseas Employment Regulations Arts 13(2)(3), 13(2)(5), 30(4), 30(19), 30(20); Greenpeace, Choppy Waters (2020)

value_label: Only employer-bought private or accident insurance is required
note: Employer-bought accident, life and medical insurance (medical cover at least NT$300,000, death cover at least NT$1.5 million, payable to the crew member); not national labor insurance.
source: Overseas Employment Regulations Art. 6(1)(3)

value_label: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
note: The 1955 hotline accepts calls, and vessels must allow crew to communicate, but access at sea is limited. Since the 18 November 2025 amendment, operators must join a wage-advance mechanism or give a bank guarantee before hiring, and report wage payments within 10 days.
source: Overseas Employment Regulations Arts 2-1, 6-1 (amended 18 Nov 2025); Ministry of Agriculture, 18 Nov 2025

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: Crew are never admitted to Taiwan as workers; no residence accrues.
source: Overseas Employment Regulations

value_label: Barred
note: Not applicable: no residence in Taiwan.
source: Overseas Employment Regulations

value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: The Labor Standards Act applies to fishing employers.
source: Labor Standards Act; Ministry of Labor

value_label: The national statutory minimum wage applies
note: The national minimum wage under the Minimum Wage Act (in force 1 Jan 2024) applies, replacing the basic wage; the reported rule allowing deductions for board and lodging was not confirmed from an official text.
source: Minimum Wage Act Art. 3; Ministry of Labor

value_label: Statutory limits on hours apply
note: Labor Standards Act hours apply in law; enforcement on board is reported to be weak.
source: Labor Standards Act; ICSF Samudra 88 (2022)

value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: Transfer only on grounds listed in Employment Service Act Art. 59 (for example closure, abuse, employer's death) or by three-party agreement. The rule requiring workers to leave Taiwan for a day before starting a new contract (Art. 52(4)) was deleted in November 2016. Total stay remains capped at 12 years (14 for qualifying home carers).
source: Employment Service Act Arts 52, 59

value_label: May form and join unions on equal terms
note: May join and form unions; the Yilan Migrant Fishermen Union was registered in 2013.
source: Trade Union Act; union records

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Broker service fees are capped by the Ministry of Labor (monthly, falling with years of service); fees in sending countries vary.
source: Ministry of Labor fee standards

value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: Labor insurance since the early 1990s and National Health Insurance; work-permit holders are enrolled in NHI at once, without the six-month wait that applies to other foreign residents.
source: Labor Insurance Act; National Health Insurance Act; Oishi and Chien (2026)

value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: 1955 hotline in five languages; local labor bureaus.
source: Ministry of Labor (official guidance)

value_label: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
note: Since 30 April 2022 migrant workers with six years' continuous service may be retained as intermediate skilled workers. Time as an ordinary migrant worker does not count toward permanent residence (Immigration Act Art. 25), so the route runs through years in the intermediate status; this reading is ours and is not stated by the Ministry. The route now rests on a new regulation in force from 30 Dec 2025, with a wage threshold of NT$35,000 a month for fishing.
source: Ministry of Labor, Long-term Retention of Migrant Workers Program (releases 17 Feb and 29 Apr 2022) and regulation of 30 Dec 2025 (official guidance); Immigration Act Arts 23, 25

value_label: Barred
note: Families of migrant workers under Employment Service Act Art. 46(1)(8)–(10) cannot obtain residence.
source: Immigration Act Art. 23(1)

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: A labor statute applies with exclusions, or a sector-specific labor statute applies
note: The Seafarers Act, a sector-specific labor statute, applies instead of the Labor Standards Act. It excludes fishing vessels under 20 tons that a Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries ordinance names.
source: Seafarers Act Art. 3(1) proviso item 3

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: A separate floor applies that is lower than, or not linked to, the national minimum
note: Wages for foreign crew are set by collective agreement between shipowners and the seafarers' union, below Korean crew; the Minister may set a seafarers' minimum wage (KRW 2,694,560 a month in 2026) and the Act draws no nationality line. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries notice setting the 2026 figure lets a collective agreement set the minimum for foreign crew, which is why the code is 1 (official guidance, not legislation).
source: Seafarers Act Art. 59; Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Notice 2025-200 (official guidance); NHRCK recommendations to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; Korea Times, 12 Jul 2023

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: Excluded from working-time rules
note: The Seafarers Act's working-time chapter (Chapter 6, including the Art. 60 hours and rest rules) does not apply to fishing vessels other than fish carriers. The Minister may set separate standards, but none were found in the Act or its Enforcement Rule. Recoded from 1 to 0 on 13 Nov 2026.
source: Seafarers Act Arts 60, 68(1)(ii), 68(2); Enforcement Rule Art. 46

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: Cannot change without the employer's consent
note: Placement runs through manning agencies; changing vessel needs the shipowner's release. Under review: the Immigration Act and the Ministry of Justice visa manual allow a change of vessel with the Ministry's prior permission on listed grounds, and no shipowner-consent rule was found in them, which would support a code of 1; the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries guideline requires repatriation when the contract ends. Editors to decide.
source: NHRCK; EJF (2024); Immigration Act; Ministry of Justice visa manual and Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries guideline (official guidance)

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: May join the Korean seafarers' union that negotiates their wages, but have little voice in it.
source: Secondary sources

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: Fees charged to the worker are prohibited in the destination's law
note: The Seafarers Act bars anyone who recruits, places or manages seafarers from taking money from them on any pretext, with no nationality limit, and penalizes breaches. Owners hiring through agencies in states outside the Maritime Labour Convention must check that the agency meets its standards. Fees charged by sending-country agencies remain an enforcement gap. Recoded from 1 to 2 on 13 Nov 2026.
source: Seafarers Act Arts 111, 113(2); World Fishing / EJF, Mar 2024

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: A statutory fishing-vessel crew accident insurance is compulsory for owners of covered vessels, replacing industrial accident insurance, with no nationality exclusion; registered foreign workers at covered workplaces are also enrolled in National Health Insurance. Distant-water and family-only vessels are excepted. Recoded from 1 to 2 on 13 Nov 2026 (coding judgment: the sector-specific statutory scheme is treated as the national scheme).
source: Fishing Vessel Crew Insurance Act Arts 6, 16; National Health Insurance Act Art. 109(2)

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
note: General labor and maritime channels. In 2026 the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family issued indicators for identifying trafficking victims (often reported as forced-labor guidelines for migrant fishers).
source: Ministry of Gender Equality and Family Notice 2026-32 (official guidance); Korea Times, 2 Sep 2026

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
note: E-10 holders may switch to the skilled-worker status (E-7-4) for long-term residence (confirmed by the Ministry of Justice, 22 Oct 2026). The Ministry's guidance sets the conditions: at least four years' stay, 200 points, annual income of KRW 25 million and Korean language level 2, with a quota of 33,000 for 2026.
source: Ministry of Justice release, 22 Oct 2026; Ministry of Justice visa manual (official guidance)

group_name: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)
value_label: Barred
note: E-10 holders are not among the statuses whose spouses and children may receive the F-3 dependant visa.
source: Immigration Act Enforcement Decree, Annex 1-2 item 25

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: A labor statute applies with exclusions, or a sector-specific labor statute applies
note: The Labor Standards Act applies, but Art. 63 excludes fisheries from its working-time, rest and holiday rules.
source: Labor Standards Act Art. 63

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: The national statutory minimum wage applies
note: The national minimum wage applies.
source: Minimum Wage Act

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: Excluded from working-time rules
note: Excluded from working-time limits by Art. 63.
source: Labor Standards Act Art. 63

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: May change workplace only on listed grounds: at most three times in the initial three years and twice in the extension; changes caused by the employer do not count.
source: Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers Art. 25(1), (4)

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: May form and join unions on equal terms
note: May form and join unions; the Supreme Court recognized the Migrants' Trade Union in 2015.
source: Supreme Court of Korea, 25 Jun 2015

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: Fees charged to the worker are prohibited in the destination's law
note: Recruitment is run by public agencies in both states; private brokers are excluded.
source: Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: National Health Insurance from the start of employment at covered workplaces, unlike the residence condition for other foreign residents; work accidents on fishing vessels are covered by the statutory fishing-vessel crew insurance rather than industrial accident insurance, and small fishery businesses must take out accident insurance for EPS workers.
source: National Health Insurance Act Art. 109(2); Fishing Vessel Crew Insurance Act Art. 6; Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers Art. 23(2); Oishi and Chien (2026)

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: Counseling line for foreign workers (1577-0071) in several languages, alongside the general 1350 labor hotline; migrant worker support centers.
source: Ministry of Employment and Labor (official guidance)

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
note: E-9 holders may switch to the skilled-worker status (E-7-4) for long-term residence (confirmed by the Ministry of Justice, 22 Oct 2026). The Ministry's guidance sets the conditions: at least four years' stay, 200 points, annual income of KRW 25 million and Korean language level 2, with a quota of 33,000 for 2026.
source: Ministry of Justice release, 22 Oct 2026; Ministry of Justice visa manual (official guidance)

group_name: South Korea · coastal fishers and aquaculture (E-9)
value_label: Barred
note: E-9 holders are not among the statuses whose spouses and children may receive the F-3 dependant visa.
source: Immigration Act Enforcement Decree, Annex 1-2 item 25

value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: The Employment Ordinance applies in full.
source: Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57)

value_label: A separate floor applies that is lower than, or not linked to, the national minimum
note: The statutory minimum wage does not apply to domestic workers who live in the household free of charge, a class wider than foreign helpers. A Minimum Allowable Wage set by government applies instead: HK$5,100 for contracts from 30 Sep 2025 and HK$5,220 for contracts signed on or after 3 Oct 2026, plus food or a food allowance.
source: Minimum Wage Ordinance (Cap. 608) s. 7(3); HKSAR press releases, 29 Sep 2025 and 2 Oct 2026

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: No statutory limit on hours (none exists for any worker in Hong Kong); a weekly rest day and statutory holidays apply.
source: Employment Ordinance Parts IV and VIII

value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: May change employer, but must normally leave Hong Kong within two weeks of the contract ending and apply from abroad; frequent changes are refused as 'job-hopping'.
source: Immigration Department, Foreign Domestic Helpers page and guidance (official guidance)

value_label: May form and join unions on equal terms
note: May form and join unions under the Trade Unions Ordinance.
source: Trade Unions Ordinance (Cap. 332)

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Agencies may charge job-seekers no more than 10% of the first month's wage.
source: Employment Agency Regulations (Cap. 57A) reg. 10(2), Second Schedule Part II

value_label: Only employer-bought private or accident insurance is required
note: Employees' compensation insurance is compulsory and the employer must provide free medical treatment; helpers are exempt from the Mandatory Provident Fund.
source: Employees' Compensation Ordinance; Standard Employment Contract (ID 407) cl. 9(a)

value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: Labour Department hotline and a dedicated portal for helpers in 12 languages.
source: fdh.labour.gov.hk (official guidance)

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: Time as a helper does not count as ordinary residence for permanent residence (Immigration Ordinance s. 2(4)(a)(vi)); upheld by the Court of Final Appeal in Vallejos (2013).
source: Immigration Ordinance (Cap. 115); Vallejos v Commissioner of Registration, FACV 19/2012 (2013)

value_label: Barred
note: Helpers may not bring dependants.
source: Immigration Department guidance (official guidance)

value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: The Labor Standards Act applies to trainees as employees.
source: Technical Intern Training Act 2016

value_label: The national statutory minimum wage applies
note: Prefectural minimum wages apply.
source: Minimum Wage Act

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: Hours, break and rest-day rules apply, except in agriculture, livestock, sericulture and fisheries; forestry is not exempt.
source: Labor Standards Act Art. 41(i) and Appended Table 1 items 6–7

value_label: Cannot change without the employer's consent
note: The current Act gives trainees no right to request a change of employer. Under Employment for Skill Development (from 1 April 2027) a worker may request a change in the same field after a period of one to two years set by ordinance, subject to skill and Japanese-language standards, with exceptions for unavoidable circumstances.
source: Technical Intern Training Act (No. 89 of 2016) Art. 19; amending Act No. 60 of 2024, Arts 8-2, 9-2

value_label: May form and join unions on equal terms
note: May form and join unions.
source: Trade Union Act

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Bilateral memoranda bind sending states to screen agencies; fees charged in sending countries are not prohibited under Japanese law. The 2027 system is to share costs with employers.
source: Memoranda of cooperation; US TIP Report 2025

value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: Enrolled in employees' health and pension insurance (all legal residents staying over three months must be enrolled). Public schemes leave a copayment of about 30%, and the government recommends supplementary private insurance for trainees.
source: Health Insurance Act; Oishi and Chien (2026)

value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: OTIT consultation in eight languages; labor inspection offices.
source: Organization for Technical Intern Training (official guidance)

value_label: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
note: Maximum five years as a trainee; may move to Specified Skilled Worker, from which (ii) can lead to permanent residence.
source: Immigration Control Act; Immigration Services Agency

value_label: Barred
note: Technical intern training is excluded from the statuses whose families may hold Dependent status.
source: Immigration Control Act, Appended Table I(4)

value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: The Labor Standards Act applies.
source: Labor Standards Act

value_label: The national statutory minimum wage applies
note: Pay must at least equal that of Japanese workers in the same job.
source: Immigration Control Act ordinances

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: Hours, break and rest-day rules apply, except in agriculture, livestock, sericulture and fisheries; forestry is not exempt.
source: Labor Standards Act Art. 41(i) and Appended Table 1 items 6–7

value_label: May change employer without the employer's consent
note: May change employer within the same field.
source: Immigration Services Agency

value_label: May form and join unions on equal terms
note: May form and join unions.
source: Trade Union Act

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Bilateral memoranda with sending states address fees; not prohibited in Japanese law.
source: Memoranda of cooperation

value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: Enrolled in employees' health insurance and employees' pension from the first day of employment at covered workplaces; the three-month residence rule applies only to National Health Insurance.
source: Health Insurance Act Arts 3, 35; Employees' Pension Insurance Act Art. 9; Oishi and Chien (2026)

value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: Registered support organizations must give consultation in the worker's language.
source: Immigration Services Agency

value_label: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
note: SSW (i) is capped at five years in total, or six with good reason, not counting time lost to pregnancy, childbirth or childcare (from 1 Apr 2026); SSW (ii) has no cap and can lead to permanent residence under the general criteria.
source: Immigration Services Agency, Specified Skilled Worker page

value_label: Only in a later status or on conditions
note: SSW (i) is excluded from the statuses whose families may hold Dependent status; SSW (ii) is not, so its holders may bring spouse and children.
source: Immigration Control Act, Appended Table I(4)
